newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slips as small cap stocks disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slips as small cap stocks disappoint.

text.p: Nasdaq shares slipped Friday, ending three consecutive days of gains, as bad news on several small capitalization stocks took center stage, analysts said.

"There's no panicky selling, but investors are very unforgiving when the news is bad. A lot of smaller companies are getting hard hit," said Jack Bayer, managing director and head of over-the-counter trader at Oppenheimer & Co.

The Nasdaq composite index lost 18.81 points or 1.53 percent to close unoffically at 1209.29. Nasdaq shares have risen in six of the previous ten sessions. Declining issues beat rising issues 2329 to 1825 on total volume of 510 million shares.

Forte Software Inc lost half its value after executives cautioned investors that the software company will spend more on sales in coming quarters, hurting the earnings outlook. Forte lost 8-5/16 to 8-5/16. Credit Acceptance Corp dropped 5-1/8 to 9-5/8 after it posted first quarter earnings of $0.26 compared to $0.20 a share on a 57 percent increase in revenue.
Gateway 2000 slipped 4-1/2 to 53-7/8 after its first quarter earnings failed to show an upside surprise.
